steps.prompt: A Data 360 Identity Resolution ruleset uses fuzzy match on Normalized Phone Number alone. Household members sharing a landline collapse into one Unified Individual, polluting consent and personalization. How should the architecture be revised?

options.label: Configure composite match criteria combining Phone with exact First Name or DOB, and preserve Unified Link DMOs for source lineage
options.rationale: Composite match rules prevent false-positive over-clustering across shared household identifiers, while Unified Link DMOs maintain full auditability to contributing source records.

options.label: Consolidate all source contact attributes directly onto the Unified Individual DMO and remove Unified Link objects to streamline joins
options.distractorAntipattern: Dropping Unified Link objects destroys record lineage and prevents downstream activations from tracing back to originating source keys.
options.rationale: Unified Link DMOs are architecturally required to maintain deterministic lineage between source records and unified profiles.

options.label: Update the profile reconciliation rule to Most Recently Updated while retaining the single-attribute fuzzy phone match criteria
options.distractorAntipattern: Reconciliation rules determine winning field values after clustering, but cannot correct erroneous cluster creation.
options.rationale: Reconciliation rules only decide which field value wins among already-matched profiles; they cannot unbundle incorrectly clustered individuals.

options.label: Replace Identity Resolution with a custom SQL Data Transform that hashes shared phone numbers into synthetic master person keys
options.distractorAntipattern: Custom key transforms bypass native graph unification, duplicate clustering logic, and do not update dynamically.
options.rationale: Manual SQL key transforms lack graph-based entity resolution, fail to handle multi-party cross-matching, and create unmaintainable custom pipeline debt.
